reason: Each FR-02 normative requirement maps to a substantive assert that fails on violation: POST 202 at tests/test_fr02.py:158, 409 state-machine guard at :170, run_id in body at :181, no shell=True at :268, GET 200 at :341, newest-first at :364, v3 columns at :448. Tautological trigger-asserts are documented methodology artifacts; the inner asserts pin the requirement. Three coverage gaps flagged: exact subprocess_exec(*shlex.split(command)) pattern, TASKQ_TASK_TIMEOUT value, and full state-machine transitions.

gaps.message: Test asserts shell=True/eval/exec source-absence only; the exact invocation pattern asyncio.create_subprocess_exec(*shlex.split(command)) is not asserted — an alternative compliant runner (e.g. subprocess.run with shell=False) would still pass.
TASKQ_TASK_TIMEOUT value is not asserted anywhere — no test verifies the subprocess is bounded by the configured timeout.

State machine pending→running→done|failed|timeout is only partially tested: the 409 conflict guard for already-running is asserted at :170, but the transitions themselves (pending→running and running→done|failed|timeout) are not asserted by any check on resulting task status.
